support.exact_excerpt: The new GenerateAlternatives procedure was actually loaded in the candidate's broad operational run. It was **not loaded in the focused context run**, which used ordinary PlanChange and still considered three structural alternatives. That round therefore tests the whole method's routing behavior, not the efficacy of the new procedure itself. Do not attribute its layout differences to a step that did not execute.

The real Prompting author read the procedure at event 10, wrote its comparison at event 23 and implemented at event 25. It considered no change, section-range reads, core plus conditional references, and a summary alongside the monolith. It chose conditional references. The baseline also produced a useful structural split. Both retained all 265 checked substantive standards lines, protected files and working local links.

Candidate improvement authoring was 13.0% faster with 6.1% fewer output tokens in this single pair. Downstream returned bytes were 15.4% higher for classification, 0.8% higher for operations and 0.2% lower for specialized skill authoring. Thus lower planning time did not produce a better loading result. Command-output bytes are a context proxy, not unique instruction tokens or billed cost.

required_constraints: Original focused-context run did not load GenerateAlternatives; ordinary PlanChange considered alternatives.
Repaired run loaded the procedure before comparison and implementation; this supports activation.
Both pass 5/5; no demonstrated loading advantage: classification bytes +15.4%, operations +0.8%, specialized -0.2%.
Returned bytes are a context proxy, not billing/unique instruction tokens; one pair does not establish general speed or creativity.
valid_alternatives: Describe bounded routing repair and preservation without loading benefit.
Use equivalent raw table values instead of percentages.
